chunks: Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, said:

And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from relieving himself, or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favour upon you so that you may be grateful.

key_terms.تَيَمَّمُوا: perform tayammum, the dry ablution with earth when water is unavailable
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: undue hardship or constriction in religious duty
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel, a state in which legal concession may apply
key_terms.صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا: clean earth or pure ground used for tayammum
key_terms.لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ: to purify you, indicating the purpose of the ruling
key_terms.مَرْضَىٰ: ill persons whose condition is recognized as a valid circumstance in the ruling
key_terms.نِعْمَتَهُ: His favour, referring to Allah’s completed blessing through guidance and law
key_terms.ٱلْغَائِطِ: relieving oneself, referring to a state requiring purification

ai.seo_question: When is tayammum allowed in Islam, and what does Qur'an 5:6 teach about it?
ai.summary: This verse sets out the ruling of tayammum when water is unavailable or its use is impeded by illness or travel. It shows that the divine law aims at purification without imposing undue hardship, and that this concession is part of Allah’s completed favour upon the believers.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from relieving himself, or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah (swt) does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favour upon you so that you may be grateful." (Surah Al-Ma’idah 5:6).
